newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares gain 1.6pct on upbeat construction.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares gain 1.6pct on upbeat construction.

text.p: Momentum carried over from Friday in construction propelled Greek shares closer to the 1,600 level on Monday.
The Athens bourse's benchmark index settled 1.65 percent or 25.95 points higher at 1,595.54, from Friday's close of 1,569.59.
It opened at 1,576.19, recording an intra-day high of 1,597.60, which is also a new year high, at the early stages of trading.
Construction were up 2.62 percent, followed by industrials and banks which firmed 1.90 percent and 1.55 percent respectively.
Friday's press reports of a new EU financial aid package for Greece in the 2000-2005 period continued to pull construction stocks higher, leading the broader market, analysts said.

The market was becoming stronger as funds were finding their way across the board, narrowing price imbalances between large cap banks and industrials on the one side and small and medium caps on the other, the analysts said.

"The market is on a clear upward channel. Shifting buying interest into all sectors besides banks and industrial blue chips provide greater support and expand the market's upside potential," said Iakovos Diamantopoulos, analyst at Hermes Brokerage.
A correction in prices will inevitably be realised, but the market's momentum suggests that this will have to wait for a while, he added.
Diamantopoulos said the 1,600 level was a mere way-point to the real psychological barrier of 1,684 points, recorded seven years ago.

"The 1,600 level constitutes a psychological barrier for as long as the index is grinding its way up towards it. The 1,600 level will be topped as easily as the 1,500 level, on course for the all-time high of 1,684 points," said Diamantopoulos.
Small-caps climbed 3.85 percent but price changes in this sector are not reflected in the bourse's general benchmark index.
Turnover continued to rise, amounting to 30.5 billion drachmas in volume of 7.6 million shares, including several blocks.
The increased contribution of block trading in overall turnover was seen by analysts as an indication of growing presence of foreign funds.
"Block trades are a finger-print of foreign buying. International funds have become more active in recent days," said Diamantopoulos.

Block trade included Elval, total 81,500 shares at 3,210 drachmas, Michaniki, 110,000 shares at 2,650, Sarantis, 89,000 shares at 3,130, as well as several blocks in Hellenic Bottling, Nat'l Mortgage Bank, and Thrace Plastics.
Advancing stocks beat decliners 158 to 79 with 24 stocks unchanged on 261 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,096-1,126. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 45 drachmas at 6,570.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $82.96-$84.66. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,219-3,435 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $20.28-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
